extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers / Scientific Review Group (study section) members, SROs, and grant review staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assigning preliminary and final numerical and non-numerical scores to NIH grant applications, including how to score individual review criteria and overall impact, use of the 1–9 scale, non-numeric designations, and procedural rules for entering and revising scores during review meeting phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9-point scoring scale (whole numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH grant application scoring system uses a 9-point scale for both overall impact scores and scores for individual review criteria. Ratings are in whole numbers only (no decimal ratings). NIH expects that scores of 1 or 9 to be used less frequently than the other scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider the full range of the rating scale and the scoring descriptors in assigning preliminary and final scores. The entire scale (1-9) should always be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact score (definition & use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall impact is the project's likelihood to have a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved and may be defined differently for different types of applications. For the overall impact score, the scale is used by all eligible (without conflict of interest) SRG members. A score of 5 is considered an average score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact score should reflect the reviewer’s overall evaluation, not a numerical average of individual criterion scores. Reviewers should feel free to assign the score that best represents impact and not feel constrained to limit scores to the upper half of the range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion scoring (typical criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases five individual criteria are scored (e.g., Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment), but certain Funding Opportunity Announcements may include more than five scored criteria. The scale is used by the assigned reviewers to evaluate (at least) these individual criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider the strengths and weaknesses within each criterion. A major strength may outweigh many minor and correctable weaknesses. Criterion scores are intended to convey how each assigned reviewer weighed the strengths and weaknesses of each section. Criterion scores are provided for all applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary scores (assigned reviewers before meeting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the review meeting, assigned reviewers determine preliminary scores for each of the scored review criteria and a preliminary score for the overall impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary impact score should reflect overall evaluation rather than an average of criterion scores. Reviewers should consider the full range of the scale but should not assume their assigned applications necessarily cover that entire range; assign scores appropriate for the work proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final scoring procedure (deliberation & private scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final scores are given by private scoring and are based on the outcome of the deliberations at the peer review meeting. Discussed applications receive numerical impact scores from all eligible reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the meeting, individual reviewer scores will be averaged and the result multiplied by 10 to determine the final impact score. The range of final application scores is 10 through 90.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact score composition (additional considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The impact score for an application is based on each individual reviewer’s assessment of the scored criteria plus additional criteria regarding the protection and inclusion of human subjects; vertebrate animal care and welfare; biohazards; and criteria specific to the funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these additional protections/ethics criteria when forming overall impact judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-numeric designation: Not Discussed (ND)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications unanimously judged by the peer review committee to be less competitive are not discussed at the peer review meeting; these applications do not receive a numerical impact score but do receive individual criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all meetings use the 'Not Discussed' option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-numeric designation: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NR/NRFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: NR occurs by majority vote of the SRG members and is used when an application lacks significant and substantial merit or presents serious ethical problems (human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents). NR-scored applications do not proceed to the second level of peer review because they cannot be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NR is a serious committee recommendation, substantially different from Not Discussed (ND).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other non-numeric codes (DF, AB, CF, NP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other non-numeric scores include DF: Deferred (usually due to lack of sufficient information or quorum, allegations of research misconduct); AB: Abstention (used rarely); CF: Conflict (score put in by a reviewer who is in conflict with the application); NP: Not Present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these codes per procedural rules when circumstances apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of critiques with scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers must enter the criterion scores into the Internet Assisted Review (IAR) site in the NIH Commons for them to appear in the summary statement. Assigned reviewers may submit criterion scores only after their critiques have been uploaded (at the SRO’s discretion, SRG members assigned as discussants may submit criterion scores without critiques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entered in IAR, the scores will be transferred to a table at the beginning of the reviewer’s critique. Providing scores without providing comments in the review critique is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: READ and EDIT phase rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In the READ phase of the meeting reviewers may submit their scores and critiques, but may not edit them. If the reviewer’s opinion changed as a result of discussion at the meeting, the reviewer should change his/her criterion scores to match his/her critiques and overall impact score as part of the EDIT phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scores and written critiques are consistent and updated after discussion when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume deletions/modifications when scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will score an application as presented in its entirety, and may not modify their scores on the assumption that a portion of the work proposed will be deleted or modified according to the SRG’s recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score the proposal as submitted, not what it might become after revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation: 1–9 descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Score descriptors map to qualitative labels: 1=Exceptional; 2=Outstanding; 3=Excellent; 4=Very Good; 5=Good; 6=Satisfactory; 7=Fair; 8=Marginal; 9=Poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A score of 5 is a good, medium-impact application. Use the descriptor table to guide what each numeric score implies about overall or criterion strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion scores are not averaged into impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The impact score for the application is not intended to be an average of criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each review criterion should be assessed based on the strength of that criterion in the context of the work being proposed; a reviewer may give moderate criterion scores but a high overall impact if one critical criterion is rated highly, or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility: an application need not be strong in all categories
rubrics_metrics.description: An application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major impact; for example, a project that by its nature is not innovative may be essential to advance a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the relative importance of criteria in context rather than expecting uniformly high scores across all criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer behavior: use of full range and airing dissenting opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are guided to use the full range of the rating scale and spread their scores to better discriminate among applications. Reviewers whose evaluations fall outside the range presented by assigned reviewers and discussants should ensure their opinions are brought to the attention of the entire committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO and Chairperson should ensure that all opinions are voiced before final scoring is conducted. Reviewers should feel free to assign the score that best represents impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion scores appear in summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The criterion scores appear in a table at the beginning of each critique in the summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure criterion scores are entered into IAR so they appear correctly in the summary statement table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring guidance applies to different application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall impact, for a research project, is defined as the project's likelihood to have a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, but may be defined differently for different types of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific guidance for Research Applications and Training Applications for any variations.
